response.sql:
WITH line_items_with_category AS (
  SELECT 
    ili.product_quantity,
    ili.derived_product_cost,
    ili.derived_total_cost,
    pc.product_type_description
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  INNER JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id
  INNER JOIN Product_Categories pc ON p.production_type_code = pc.production_type_code
),
category_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    product_type_description,
    AVG(CAST(product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4))) as avg_quantity,
    AVG(ABS(derived_product_cost - derived_total_cost)) as avg_cost_difference
  FROM line_items_with_category
  GROUP BY product_type_description
),
mean_cost_difference AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_cost_difference) as mean_cd FROM category_averages
),
filtered_categories AS (
  SELECT 
    ca.avg_quantity,
    ca.avg_cost_difference,
    mcd.mean_cd
  FROM category_averages ca
  CROSS JOIN mean_cost_difference mcd
  WHERE ca.avg_cost_difference > mcd.mean_cd
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_quantity),
  AVG(avg_cost_difference),
  AVG(avg_cost_difference - mean_cd)
FROM filtered_categories;

assumptions.assumption: `product_quantity` is VARCHAR(50) but contains numeric values that can be cast to DECIMAL—the query casts it for averaging
INNER JOINs should be used to exclude unmatched rows (lines with no product or category match)
The AVG() function's standard behavior (ignoring NULLs) is the intended interpretation of 'ignore missing values'

alternatives.interpretation: Stricter NULL handling: exclude entire rows from category calculations if any of product_quantity, derived_product_cost, or derived_total_cost are NULL, rather than letting AVG() skip individual NULLs
